message.content:
You are reworking two designs on PR #1772 of Lock Code Manager (a Home Assistant custom integration). The branch is `feat/password-config`, in worktree `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.worktrees/password-config`, HEAD 31cdae3c. The PR puts a user's password in the configuration beside their PIN.

First read `/tmp/lcm-pr2b/context.md` (project rules, report format) and follow it, and `/tmp/lcm-pr2b/head.md`. The PR is open, so **never amend**: add new commits. **Do not push.**

**Why:** four review rounds kept finding new facets of two designs. Raman chose to redesign them rather than patch the facets. Each rework replaces code; it does not add special cases. Delete what the new design makes unnecessary.

## Rework 1: Password entities are reconciled, not tracked per lock event
Today `text.py` adds a slot's Password entity from per-lock events: `register_lock_added_handler`, `register_lock_removed_handler` (with an "exclude the removed lock" rule and a LOADED guard), a `with_password` set, and a discard on slot add. Each event sees the lock set mid-change, and that caused these bugs:
- a reused slot number got no entity back;
- an unload queued removals;
- removing two password locks in one options submit leaves every Password entity behind, because each handler counts the other leaving lock as remaining (`_async_release_locks` calls the handlers before `async_unload_lock` pops the locks);
- a swap of password locks in one update can race the fire-and-forget removal.

**New design:** one reconcile step makes each slot's Password entity match `CredentialType.PASSWORD in available_credential_types(entry)`: add the missing ones, remove the extra ones. It runs once the update pass has settled the lock set and the slots, i.e. after `_async_release_locks` and `_async_setup_new_locks` and after new slots get their standard entities (read `async_update_listener`'s update pass in `__init__.py`). It is the single place that decides, and it is idempotent.
- How the text platform exposes it is your call. A callback registered on the entry's `EntityCallbackRegistry` (the way adders are registered), which the update pass invokes at the end, fits the code's pattern. Removal must be awaited, not fire-and-forget, so an add in the same pass cannot race it.
- Keep: the stored password stays when the entity goes (decision 10); a new slot gets the entity when the entry offers passwords.
- Remove the per-lock handlers, the `with_password` bookkeeping, the LOADED guard and the "exclude the removed lock" logic, if the reconcile makes them unnecessary. Unload must not remove registry entries beyond what the existing slot teardown already does.
- Leave capability changes after setup to PR 4. Make the reconcile a function PR 4 can call when capabilities refresh, and say so in its docstring.

Tests (the existing Password-entity tests must still pass):
- **New:** an entry with two Virtual-type password locks plus the PIN-only mock lock; one options submit removes both password locks; afterwards no slot has a Password entity, and the stored passwords remain. Build two password locks from the existing fixtures (see how `test_the_password_entity_stays_while_a_password_lock_remains` builds a two-lock entry). If a second Virtual lock is impractical, report what you tried rather than writing a test that doesn't reach the case.
- **New:** a swap in one submit, removing the password lock and adding another, leaves exactly one Password entity per slot, with no duplicate unique-id error in `caplog`.
- Mutation: reconcile on per-lock events instead (or skip the reconcile), and the multi-removal test must fail.

## Rework 2: the refusal rule asks one precise question
Read Raman's decision 11, made precise on 2026-10-25, in `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-password-credential-design.md`: "A refused value holds only its own credential, with a repair, while the user has another credential in sync on the refusing lock; otherwise the user is turned off. `slot_disabled` is answered when the user re-enables."

Today `_keeps_another_credential` in `ha/runtime.py` reads the configuration (`coordinator.wants`) with an exception for credentials the same lock holds refused. These kept slipping through:
- a credential the refusing lock doesn't take;
- a suspended (`CANT_SET`) password;
- a not-yet-written one.

**New rule:** when a lock refuses a value for a slot, the user stays on only if another address of that slot on **that lock's worker** has status `IN_SYNC` and a non-None want (a credential actually working there). Replace `_keeps_another_credential`; don't add another exception to it.

**`slot_disabled` is answered when the user re-enables the slot:** delete the `slot_disabled_{entry}_{slot}` issue in the coordinator's successful enable (`async_request_active_toggle(True)`), where `credential_required` is already deleted. Remove the in-sync-based `slot_disabled` deletion from `async_reconcile_issues` (the `wanted` predicate) if nothing else needs it. A repeat refusal raises its own repair again through the normal path. Check the existing `slot_disabled` tests: one that expects deletion once the PIN is back in sync may need to re-enable explicitly. If its scenario no longer makes sense, report it rather than forcing it.

Tests:
- **A suspended password is no fallback:** on the Virtual entry, make the password write fail until it is suspended (`CANT_SET`; see how other tests drive a slot to suspended), then the lock refuses the PIN. The user is turned off.
- **A credential the refusing lock doesn't take is no fallback:** the PIN-only mock lock refuses the PIN of a user who also has a stored password. The user is turned off. If the mock lock fixture makes this hard, use the Virtual entry with the password address absent from the worker.
- **The existing "refused password while the PIN works" test still holds:** the PIN is in sync on that lock, so the user stays on.
- **Re-enable answers `slot_disabled`.** A user whose only credential is refused is turned off with `slot_disabled`. Re-enabling deletes that issue, even if the same PIN is then refused again, which raises a fresh repair through the normal path. Assert the state after each step.
- **Mutations:**
  - Count a non-IN_SYNC address as a fallback: the suspended test must fail.
  - Read the configuration instead of the worker: the doesn't-take test must fail.
  - Drop the enable-time deletion: the re-enable test must fail.

## Fix 3: the edit form decides "offered" once per dialog
`config_flow.py`: `_password_offered` is recomputed each time the edit form is shown, including a re-show after an error. So a password the user cleared can come back if the answer flips between the error and the next submit. Decide it on the first show of the flow only, and keep it for re-shows. Test: patch `_offers_password` to answer True and then False across an error re-show, and assert a cleared password stays cleared. Mutation: recompute on re-show, and the test must fail.

Commit each rework and the fix separately, with test-first where possible. Then run the full suite with `-n auto`. The paced tests `TestPacing`, `test_pins_changed_while_the_lock_is_offline_reach_it_once_each_paced` and `test_a_paced_test_keeps_the_real_delay_between_operations` flake in parallel; re-run any failure on its own. Then run `prek run --all-files`.

In your report, list exactly what code each rework **removed**, as well as what it added. Use the format context.md gives, with SHAs.

# Claude Code Global Context

`CLAUDE.md` directives are scoped to contexts through headings and subheadings. Always follow the following directives:

- If a directive is vague, ask for clarification instead of making an assumption.
- When relevant to a chat generated directive (e.g. not `CLAUDE.md` directives), suggest installed plugins that require explicit activation because I may not think to use it.
- Any directives that modify files local to the context are approved and should not require further input from me to implement.
- If in a local git repo with a remote that I don't own and `.claude/` is not already excluded in `.gitignore`, exclude it so that we don't leak our directives to the project. If `.claude/` already exists, any directives for `CLAUDE.md`

## MCP usage

- Use `serena` MCP for semantic code retrieval and editing tools
  - Call `onboarding` and `initial_instructions` tools first if needed

## Code style

### Defining a preferred code style in ./.claude/CLAUDE.md

- If preferred code style is already defined, ignore this directive, else when working in a new local git repository (e.g. this is the first session in this path specific local repo) tied to a parent project (e.g. a Home Assistant custom integration), and code styles don't match between parent and local, ask which code style to prefer and add that directive so that this directive is skipped next time.
- If I am first contributing to a project that is not mine and I have a conflict code style from the project's, ask which is preferred and add that directive.

## Python

- Prefer `uv` over `pip` for package, virtual environment, and "tool" (project-less python apps) management
- Prefer imports from canonical/top-level modules over submodules (e.g., use `from package import X` not `from package.submodule import X` when both work). However, DO move imports to a different top-level module if that's where the symbol is canonically defined (e.g., `ConfigEntryError` belongs in `exceptions`, not re-exported from `config_entries`)

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. ## Rework 1: Password entities are reconciled, not tracked per lock event
Today `text.py` adds a slot's Password entity from per-lock events: `register_lock_added_handler`, `register_lock_removed_handler` (with an "exclude the removed lock" rule and a LOADED guard), a `with_password` set, and a discard on slot add. Each event sees the lock set mid-change, and that caused these bugs:
- a reused slot number got no entity back;
- an unload queued removals;
- removing two password locks in one options submit leaves every Password entity behind, because each handler counts the other leaving lock as remaining (`_async_release_locks` calls the handlers before `async_unload_lock` pops the locks);
- a swap of password locks in one update can race the fire-and-forget removal.

**New design:** one reconcile step makes each slot's Password entity match `CredentialType.PASSWORD in available_credential_types(entry)`: add the missing ones, remove the extra ones. It runs once the update pass has settled the lock set and the slots, i.e. after `_async_release_locks` and `_async_setup_new_locks` and after new slots get their standard entities (read `async_update_listener`'s update pass in `__init__.py`). It is the single place that decides, and it is idempotent.
- How the text platform exposes it is your call. A callback registered on the entry's `EntityCallbackRegistry` (the way adders are registered), which the update pass invokes at the end, fits the code's pattern. Removal must be awaited, not fire-and-forget, so an add in the same pass cannot race it.
- Keep: the stored password stays when the entity goes (decision 10); a new slot gets the entity when the entry offers passwords.
- Remove the per-lock handlers, the `with_password` bookkeeping, the LOADED guard and the "exclude the removed lock" logic, if the reconcile makes them unnecessary. Unload must not remove registry entries beyond what the existing slot teardown already does.
- Leave capability changes after setup to PR 4. Make the reconcile a function PR 4 can call when capabilities refresh, and say so in its docstring.

## Rework 2: the refusal rule asks one precise question
Read Raman's decision 11, made precise on 2026-10-25, in `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-password-credential-design.md`: "A refused value holds only its own credential, with a repair, while the user has another credential in sync on the refusing lock; otherwise the user is turned off. `slot_disabled` is answered when the user re-enables."

Today `_keeps_another_credential` in `ha/runtime.py` reads the configuration (`coordinator.wants`) with an exception for credentials the same lock holds refused. These kept slipping through:

# Shared context for every PR 2b task

You are implementing one task of an 11-task plan in Lock Code Manager, a Home Assistant custom integration that keeps lock credentials in sync. The sync core already keeps one address per (slot, credential type) and each lock takes PIN plus, on the Virtual provider, password (PR 2a, merged as #1770). Nothing could configure a password until now. PR 2b puts the password in the user's configuration and opens every user-facing write path to it: the text entity, the actions (`set_credential`, `clear_credential`, `add_user`), the config flow and its YAML path. Only Virtual takes passwords until a later Z-Wave PR.

The plan's header (goal, architecture, ground rules, the plan's own decisions and the file map) is in `/tmp/lcm-pr2b/head.md`. Read it first. Your task's full text is in `/tmp/lcm-pr2b/task<N>.md`. Do not read the full plan.

## Where to work

- Worktree: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.worktrees/password-config` (branch `feat/password-config`). Use **absolute paths** for every edit. The main checkout at `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager` is on another branch, and you must not touch it. Run commands from the worktree, with `cd <worktree> && ...` in each command.
- Python: `/Users/raman/projects/lock_code_manager/.venv/bin/python`. Dependencies are already installed.
- **Type check:** `prek run mypy --all-files`, run from the worktree. Do **not** use `python -m mypy` from the venv: it reports about 113 errors on untouched main.
- Tests: `$PY -m pytest <paths> -q -p no:cacheprovider`. Run targeted files plus anything that greps as depending on what you changed; the whole suite runs in Task 11.

## Project rules (they override general habits)

- Match the surrounding code's style. Its docstrings and comments are terse prose that states intent. No Google-style `Args:`/`Returns:` sections. Comments say why, not history ("this used to be..."). Spell out acronyms in comments.
- No inline or function-local imports. No `nonlocal` or `global`. Prefer comprehensions and `next()` over loops with a flag. Use `@override` on overriding methods (mypy enforces it).
- `sync/` must import nothing from the rest of the package (`tests/test_architecture.py`). `model/` must not import `ha/` or `providers/`.

# Password PR 2b: password in the configuration — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A user can hold a password as well as, or instead of, a PIN. It is stored in their configuration, set from a text entity, the config flow and the actions, and Lock Code Manager keeps it in sync on every lock that takes passwords (Virtual only until PR 4).

**Architecture:** The core already keeps one address per (slot, credential type) and wants nothing for a password (PR 2a, #1770). This PR gives the password a configuration field (`password`, beside `pin`), makes the slot coordinator want it, and opens every user-facing write path to it: the text entity, `set_credential`/`clear_credential`/`add_user`, the config flow and the setup YAML. The credential-required rule becomes "at least one credential of any type". A refused value holds only its own credential unless it was the user's only one (spec decision 11). Duplicates are refused at configuration time for both types (decision 12).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-password-credential-design.md` (decisions 4, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12; sections "Configuration and the credential-required rule", "Entities and validation", "Services and websocket").

## Decisions this plan makes (raise with Raman if any is wrong)

1. **The PIN keeps today's character rules.** The spec's validator says "digits for PIN". This PR adds the password rule only: refusing non-digit PINs would break users whose locks accept them (the User Code CC alphanumeric follow-up in the spec's "Out" list). The validator is shaped so a PIN rule is one line later.
2. **Password length is checked in characters.** `_validate_credential_length` compares `len(value)` against `length_bounds(type)` for every type. Z-Wave's byte limits (spec decision 1) become character limits in the Z-Wave provider's capabilities in PR 4 (`max_length // 2`). Recorded in the carryover file in Task 11.
3. **The config flow shows a Password field only when the entry offers passwords.** In the subentry flows (add a user, edit a user) the field appears when a lock in the entry takes passwords. The setup flow's form has no locks set up yet, so it has no Password field; its YAML path accepts `password:`. Editing a user whose password is stored but not offered keeps it (decision 10).
4. **`mask_pin` stays; `mask_credential` is added.** A PIN's token is unchanged (`pin#…`), so existing logs still deobfuscate. A password's token is `pwd#…`, salted with its type, so a PIN and a password with the same value mask differently.
5. **A refused value's repair** reuses the per-lock `slot_suspended_*` issue id with a new translation key, `credential_refused`, so acknowledging it resumes the credential (the existing `ResumeSlotRepairFlow`).
6. **A duplicate is refused only when the value changes.** Editing a user whose PIN already matches another user's (a configuration saved before this rule) does not fail on the untouched PIN.

tools.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content: markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema. Use it when the request identifies a page and needs its content or defined fields: the user gives a URL or names a page or PDF and wants it read or summarized, or wants prices, specs, contact details or a table from it. Use `firecrawl_search` when additional web sources are needed; on an authenticated session, `firecrawl_map` lists a site's URLs and `firecrawl_crawl` collects a set of pages.

Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch or a smaller `maxAge` to bound staleness. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. Browser actions can change the live page when interactive actions are enabled. Authenticated responses can include a `metadata.scrapeId` for optional scrape feedback.

On an authenticated session, `firecrawl_search` and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching provider returns typed records in one call.

With `alexandria` in place of `url`, the tool runs catalogued provider capabilities instead of fetching a page. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

tools.name: mcp__mcphub-automation__firecrawl-firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search web, news, or image sources and return ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Use it for current information, or to list businesses, people, products, jobs or events with websites, prices or contacts. Each web result is a title, URL, and description; use `firecrawl_scrape` on a result URL when the excerpt is not enough.

Authenticated search also returns matching Alexandria data providers in data.tools (companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more). Prefer a provider over scraping pages when the task needs the same fields across several entities, exact figures or timestamps, provenance, or many records; use web results when they already answer the question. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only.

On an authenticated session, tool matches describe available capabilities; `firecrawl_find_tools` returns their contracts and `firecrawl_scrape` with an `alexandria` body executes a selected capability. Keyless sessions get no Alexandria matches in data.tools.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`; its hits return in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`. For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns hits in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; authenticated sessions also have `firecrawl_gov_search` as the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law. `categories: ["research"]` restricts web results to research-affiliated websites; the `firecrawl_research_*` tools are a separate surface over paper abstracts and full text (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, arXiv). Returns source-type result groups and usage metadata. Authenticated responses can include an `id` for optional search feedback.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. import logging
from typing import override

from homeassistant.components.text import TextEntity, TextMode
from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntryState
from homeassistant.const import CONF_NAME
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant, callback
from homeassistant.exceptions import ServiceValidationError
from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er
from homeassistant.helpers.entity_platform import AddEntitiesCallback

from .const import DOMAIN
from .entity import BaseLockCodeManagerEntity
from .ha.entry import LockCodeManagerConfigEntry, available_credential_types
from .ha.slot_coordinator import InvalidNameError
from .model.credentials import CredentialType
from .model.queries import get_entry_config, subentry_id_for_slot
from .providers import BaseLock

_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)


async def async_setup_entry(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
    async_add_entities: AddEntitiesCallback,
) -> bool:
    """Set up config entry."""
    runtime_data = config_entry.runtime_data
    callbacks = runtime_data.callbacks
    # Slots with a password entity now: the type follows the entry's locks.
    with_password: set[int] = set()

    @callback
    def add_password_entity(slot_num: int, ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry) -> None:
        if slot_num in with_password:
            return
        with_password.add(slot_num)
        async_add_entities(
            [
                LockCodeManagerCredentialText(
                    hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num, CredentialType.PASSWORD
                )
            ],
            True,
            config_subentry_id=subentry_id_for_slot(config_entry, slot_num),
        )

    @callback
    def add_standard_text_entities(slot_num: int, ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry) -> None:
        """Add a slot's name and PIN, and its password if the entry offers one."""
        # A number issued again: its earlier password entity left with the
        # slot that held it.
        with_password.discard(slot_num)
        async_add_entities(
            [
                LockCodeManagerNameText(hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num),
                LockCodeManagerCredentialText(
                    hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num, CredentialType.PIN
                ),
            ],
            True,
            config_subentry_id=subentry_id_for_slot(config_entry, slot_num),
        )
        if CredentialType.PASSWORD in available_credential_types(config_entry):
            add_password_entity(slot_num, ent_reg)

    @callback
    def locks_added(locks: list[BaseLock]) -> None:
        if not any(
            CredentialType.PASSWORD in lock.managed_credential_types for lock in locks
        ):
            return
        ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
        for slot_num in get_entry_config(config_entry).slot_numbers:
            add_password_entity(slot_num, ent_reg)

    @callback
    def lock_removed(lock_entity_id: str) -> None:
        # Unloading runs these handlers too, but its slot teardown has already
        # removed every slot entity; only a lock leaving a loaded entry acts.
        if config_entry.state is not ConfigEntryState.LOADED:
            return
        # The removed lock is still held while its handlers run.
        remaining = (
            lock
            for entity_id, lock in runtime_data.locks.items()
            if entity_id != lock_entity_id
        )
        if any(
            CredentialType.PASSWORD in lock.managed_credential_types
            for lock in remaining
        ):
            return
        for slot_num in sorted(with_password):
            with_password.discard(slot_num)
            config_entry.async_create_task(
                hass,
                callbacks.async_remove_entity(f"{slot_num}|password"),
                f"Remove slot {slot_num} password entity",
            )

    config_entry.async_on_unload(
        callbacks.register_standard_adder(add_standard_text_entities)
    )
    config_entry.async_on_unload(callbacks.register_lock_added_handler(locks_added))
    config_entry.async_on_unload(callbacks.register_lock_removed_handler(lock_removed))
    return True


class LockCodeManagerText(BaseLockCodeManagerEntity, TextEntity):
    """A slot's text field; each subclass owns its write."""

    # Defaults for keys with no length constraint (the slot name) and the
    # fallback when bound locks advertise nothing or an unsatisfiable range.
    _DEFAULT_MIN = 0
    _DEFAULT_MAX = 9999

    def __init__(
        self,
        hass: HomeAssistant,
        ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,
        config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
        slot_num: int,
        key: str,
        text_mode: TextMode,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize Text entity."""
        BaseLockCodeManagerEntity.__init__(
            self, hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num, key
        )
        self._attr_mode = text_mode

    @property
    @override
    def native_min(self) -> int:
        """
        Return the minimum value length -- always the permissive default.

        The advertised per-lock minimum is deliberately NOT surfaced here.
        Home Assistant's ``text.set_value`` service rejects
        ``len(value) < native_min`` before the value reaches the coordinator,
        which would block the empty string that clears a slot and would replace
        the coordinator's per-lock error with a generic one. The coordinator
        (``SlotEntityCoordinator._validate_credential_length``) is the
        authoritative minimum gate; an empty PIN is exempt because it clears
        the slot.
        """
        return self._DEFAULT_MIN

    @property
    @override
    def native_max(self) -> int:
        """
        Return the maximum value length -- always the permissive default.

        The advertised maximum is deliberately NOT surfaced here, for the same
        reason as the minimum. Home Assistant turns ``native_max`` into the
        field's ``maxlength``, so a lock advertising a limit lower than it
        really accepts would stop the keystrokes with no message at all: the
        field simply refuses to grow and nothing says why. The coordinator
        refuses the write instead, naming the lock and the range it claims,
        which is what somebody needs to see to recognise a bad advertisement.
        """
        return self._DEFAULT_MAX

    @property
    @override
    def native_value(self) -> str | None:
        """Return native value."""
        return self._state

    @override
    async def async_added_to_hass(self) -> None:
        """Handle entity added to hass."""
        await BaseLockCodeManagerEntity.async_added_to_hass(self)
        await TextEntity.async_added_to_hass(self)


class LockCodeManagerNameText(LockCodeManagerText):
    """A slot's name."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        hass: HomeAssistant,
        ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,
        config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
        slot_num: int,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the name entity."""
        super().__init__(
            hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num, CONF_NAME, TextMode.TEXT
        )

    @override
    async def async_set_value(self, value: str) -> None:
        """Rename the slot's user."""
        coordinator = self._require_slot_coordinator()
        try:
            await coordinator.async_request_name_update(value)
        except InvalidNameError as err:
            raise ServiceValidationError(
                translation_domain=DOMAIN,
                translation_key=err.error_key,
                translation_placeholders=err.placeholders,
            ) from err
        self.async_write_ha_state()


class LockCodeManagerCredentialText(LockCodeManagerText):
    """
    One of a slot's credentials, keyed by its type.

    Sets no ``pattern``: Home Assistant's own refusal quotes the value
    (spec decision 6). The coordinator is the gate for every rule but one.
    Home Assistant caps a text entity at 255 characters whatever its
    ``native_max``, and ``text.set_value`` refuses a longer value before this
    entity sees it, with an error that quotes it. That is a limit of Home
    Assistant this integration cannot close.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        hass: HomeAssistant,
        ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry,
        config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
        slot_num: int,
        credential_type: CredentialType,
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize the credential entity."""
        super().__init__(
            hass,
            ent_reg,
            config_entry,
            slot_num,
            credential_type.value,
            TextMode.PASSWORD,
        )
        self.credential_type = credential_type

    @override
    async def async_set_value(self, value: str) -> None:
        """Set or clear the credential."""
        await self._require_slot_coordinator().async_request_credential_update(
            self.credential_type, value
        )
        self.async_write_ha_state()

"""
Typed callback registry for entity lifecycle management.

Platforms register entity-creation callbacks; entities register
their own removal callbacks.
"""

import asyncio
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
import logging
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Protocol

from homeassistant.core import callback
from homeassistant.helpers import entity_registry as er

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from ..providers import BaseLock

_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class StandardEntityCallback(Protocol):
    """Protocol for callbacks that create standard slot entities (one per slot)."""

    def __call__(self, slot_num: int, ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry) -> None:
        """Create entities for a slot."""
        ...


class LockSlotEntityCallback(Protocol):
    """Protocol for callbacks that create lock-slot entities (one per lock+slot)."""

    def __call__(
        self, lock: BaseLock, slot_num: int, ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry
    ) -> None:
        """Create entities for a lock+slot combination."""
        ...


class LockUpdateCallback(Protocol):
    """Protocol for callbacks that handle lock additions."""

    def __call__(self, locks: list[BaseLock]) -> None:
        """Handle lock additions."""
        ...


class LockRemoveCallback(Protocol):
    """Protocol for callbacks that handle lock removal."""

    def __call__(self, lock_entity_id: str) -> None:
        """Handle lock removal."""
        ...


# Type alias for entity removal callbacks (async)
EntityRemoveCallback = Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]

# Type alias for unregister functions
UnregisterFunc = Callable[[], None]


@dataclass
class EntityCallbackRegistry:
    """
    Registry of entity lifecycle callbacks.

    Entity Types:
        Standard: Entities created once per slot (e.g., enabled switch, name/PIN
            text fields, event sensor, active binary sensor). These exist for
            every configured slot.

        Lock-slot: Entities created once per lock+slot combination (e.g., PIN
            code sensor showing the actual code on the lock, in-sync binary
            sensor). For 3 locks with 2 slots, this creates 6 entities.
    """

    # Entity creation callbacks (platforms register these in async_setup_entry)
    add_standard_entity: list[StandardEntityCallback] = field(default_factory=list)
    add_lock_slot_entity: list[LockSlotEntityCallback] = field(default_factory=list)

    # Entity removal callbacks (entities register themselves in async_added_to_hass)
    # Key format: "{slot_num}|{key}" or "{slot_num}|{key}|{lock_entity_id}"
    remove_entity: dict[str, EntityRemoveCallback] = field(default_factory=dict)

    # Lock lifecycle callbacks (entities register to be notified of lock changes)
    lock_added: list[LockUpdateCallback] = field(default_factory=list)
    lock_removed: list[LockRemoveCallback] = field(default_factory=list)

    def register_standard_adder(
        self, callback: StandardEntityCallback
    ) -> UnregisterFunc:
        """
        Register callback for adding standard slot entities.

        Used by: switch, text, event, binary_sensor (active sensor)
        """
        self.add_standard_entity.append(callback)
        return lambda: (
            self.add_standard_entity.remove(callback)
            if callback in self.add_standard_entity
            else None
        )

    def register_lock_slot_adder(
        self, callback: LockSlotEntityCallback
    ) -> UnregisterFunc:
        """
        Register callback for adding lock-slot entities.

        Used by: sensor (PIN code), binary_sensor (in-sync)
        """
        self.add_lock_slot_entity.append(callback)
        return lambda: (
            self.add_lock_slot_entity.remove(callback)
            if callback in self.add_lock_slot_entity
            else None
        )

    def register_entity_remover(
        self, uid: str, callback: EntityRemoveCallback
    ) -> UnregisterFunc:
        """
        Register callback for entity removal by unique ID.

        Entities call this in async_added_to_hass to register themselves
        for removal when their slot/key is removed from config.
        """
        self.remove_entity[uid] = callback

        def unregister() -> None:
            self.remove_entity.pop(uid, None)

        return unregister

    def register_lock_added_handler(
        self, callback: LockUpdateCallback
    ) -> UnregisterFunc:
        """Register callback for lock addition notifications."""
        self.lock_added.append(callback)
        return lambda: (
            self.lock_added.remove(callback) if callback in self.lock_added else None
        )

    def register_lock_removed_handler(
        self, callback: LockRemoveCallback
    ) -> UnregisterFunc:
        """Register callback for lock removal notifications."""
        self.lock_removed.append(callback)
        return lambda: (
            self.lock_removed.remove(callback)
            if callback in self.lock_removed
            else None
        )

    @callback
    def invoke_standard_adders(self, slot_num: int, ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry) -> None:
        """Invoke all standard entity creation callbacks."""
        for cb in self.add_standard_entity:
            try:
                cb(slot_num, ent_reg)
            except Exception:
                _LOGGER.exception(
                    "Error in standard entity callback for slot %s", slot_num
                )

    @callback
    def invoke_lock_slot_adders(
        self, lock: BaseLock, slot_num: int, ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry
    ) -> None:
        """Invoke all lock-slot entity creation callbacks."""
        for cb in self.add_lock_slot_entity:
            try:
                cb(lock, slot_num, ent_reg)
            except Exception:
                _LOGGER.exception(
                    "Error in lock-slot entity callback for lock %s slot %s",
                    lock.lock.entity_id,
                    slot_num,
                )

    async def invoke_entity_removers_for_slot(self, slot_num: int) -> None:
        """
        Invoke entity removal callbacks for an entire slot.

        Removers are independent and run concurrently; one that raises is
        logged and does not keep the rest from running.
        """
        prefix = f"{slot_num}|"
        to_remove = [uid for uid in self.remove_entity if uid.startswith(prefix)]
        async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
            for uid in to_remove:
                tg.create_task(self._remove_entity(uid))

    async def async_remove_entity(self, uid: str) -> None:
        """Remove the one entity registered as ``uid``, if there is one."""
        if uid in self.remove_entity:
            await self._remove_entity(uid)

    async def _remove_entity(self, uid: str) -> None:
        """Run one entity remover, logging rather than raising."""
        try:
            await self.remove_entity[uid]()
        except Exception:
            _LOGGER.exception("Error removing entity with uid %s", uid)
        finally:
            self.remove_entity.pop(uid, None)

    @callback
    def invoke_lock_added_handlers(self, locks: list[BaseLock]) -> None:
        """Invoke lock-added callbacks."""
        for cb in self.lock_added:
            try:
                cb(locks)
            except Exception:
                _LOGGER.exception("Error in lock added callback")

    @callback
    def invoke_lock_removed_handlers(self, lock_entity_id: str) -> None:
        """
        Invoke lock-removed callbacks.

        Iterates a snapshot of the handler list because handlers may
        unregister themselves (or other handlers) during invocation.
        """
        for cb in list(self.lock_removed):
            try:
                cb(lock_entity_id)
            except Exception:
                _LOGGER.exception(
                    "Error in lock removed callback for %s", lock_entity_id
                )

    async def _setup_one_lock(lock_entity_id: str) -> BaseLock | None:
        # Every slot's want goes in with the hold: a new worker reads them all
        # in its first exchange.
        wants = {
            slot_num: coordinator.wants
            for slot_num, coordinator in runtime_data.slot_coordinators.items()
        }
        # Holding waits on the lock's provider setup, which has the operation
        # deadline to answer; said long before that.
        still_waiting = hass.loop.call_later(
            SETUP_WAIT_WARNING_SECONDS,
            _LOGGER.warning,
            "%s (%s): still waiting for %s to answer its setup; its "
            "entities come once it does",
            entry_id,
            entry_title,
            lock_entity_id,
        )
        try:
            lock = await async_hold_lock(hass, config_entry, lock_entity_id, wants)
        except Exception as err:
            # Transport failures degrade inside async_setup_internal, and
            # structural validation failures are logged there and kept
            # degraded, so a popped lock is either a genuine bug or a lock
            # whose provider stopped resolving between selection and setup --
            # an mqtt device re-discovered under an unrecognized bridge. The
            # config flow refuses that selection, so it cannot arrive here
            # from the selection path.
            _LOGGER.error(
                "%s (%s): Failed to set up lock %s: %s",
                entry_id,
                entry_title,
                lock_entity_id,
                err,
                exc_info=err,
            )
            if isinstance(err, UnclaimedLockError):
                # Only this failure has a diagnosis and an action to offer.
                # Any other exception is a bug in a provider LCM does speak,
                # and a repair telling that user their bridge is unsupported
                # sends them to remove a lock that works.
                _async_report_dropped_lock(hass, lock_entity_id, err)
            return None
        finally:
            still_waiting.cancel()
        runtime_data.locks[lock_entity_id] = lock
        # A want that changed while the hold waited -- a condition entity
        # turning, say -- was told only to the locks the entry held then.
        for slot_num, coordinator in runtime_data.slot_coordinators.items():
            if coordinator.wants != wants.get(slot_num):
                coordinator.async_push_want([lock_entity_id])
        _LOGGER.debug("%s (%s): Holding lock %s", entry_id, entry_title, lock_entity_id)
        async_delete_issue(
            hass, DOMAIN, per_lock_issue_id("lock_dropped", lock_entity_id)
        )
        # This lock's entities now, not once every lock is held: holding waits
        # on the lock's provider setup, which a lock that does not answer can
        # stretch to the operation deadline.
        for slot_num in new_config.slot_numbers:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "%s (%s): Adding lock %s slot %s sensor and event entity",
                entry_id,
                entry_title,
                lock_entity_id,
                slot_num,
            )
            callbacks.invoke_lock_slot_adders(lock, slot_num, ent_reg)
        callbacks.invoke_lock_added_handlers([lock])
        return lock

    # Set up locks concurrently. Each lock's initial usercode fetch can take
    # seconds (Z-Wave node poll, Schlage HTTP, Matter device read); serial
    # setup meant lock N+1 only began once lock N finished. Each lock handles
    # its own failure, so one bad lock does not cancel the others; a
    # cancellation still propagates, so Home Assistant shutting down is not
    # mistaken for a lock that could not be set up.
    async with asyncio.TaskGroup() as tg:
        tasks = [
            tg.create_task(_setup_one_lock(lock_entity_id))
            for lock_entity_id in locks_to_add
        ]
    for task in tasks:
        # A task group lets a cancelled child go: Home Assistant stopping.
        task.result()

async def _settled(hass: HomeAssistant) -> None:
    worker = lock_registry(hass).worker(VIRTUAL_LOCK_ENTITY_ID)
    assert worker is not None
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    await worker.settled()


async def test_an_entry_with_a_password_lock_offers_passwords(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """The entry's types are the union of what its locks take."""
    assert available_credential_types(lcm_config_entry) == {
        CredentialType.PIN,
        CredentialType.PASSWORD,
    }


async def test_a_configured_password_reaches_the_lock(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """Set through the coordinator, the password is written beside the PIN."""
    coordinator = lcm_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]

    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(
        CredentialType.PASSWORD, "open sesame"
    )
    await _settled(hass)

    lock = get_virtual_lock(hass, lcm_config_entry)
    assert lock._data["1"]["password"] == "open sesame"
    assert lock._data["1"]["code"] == "1234"
    assert get_entry_config(lcm_config_entry).slot(1)["password"] == "open sesame"

    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """Passwords are not stripped (spec decision 7)."""
    coordinator = lcm_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]

    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PASSWORD, " pw ")
    await _settled(hass)

    assert get_virtual_lock(hass, lcm_config_entry)._data["1"]["password"] == " pw "

    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """Spaces alone are refused, not kept as typed, and nothing is stored."""
    coordinator = lcm_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]

    with pytest.raises(ServiceValidationError, match="Password must not be blank"):
        await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(
            CredentialType.PASSWORD, "   "
        )

    assert "password" not in get_entry_config(lcm_config_entry).slot(1)


async def test_clearing_the_password_leaves_the_slot_on(
    hass: HomeAssistant, lcm_config_entry
) -> None:
    """The PIN remains: the slot stays enabled (spec decision 4)."""
    coordinator = lcm_config_entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1]
    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PASSWORD, "pw")
    await _settled(hass)

    assert coordinator.is_active is True

    await coordinator.async_request_credential_update(CredentialType.PIN, "")

    async def _setup_one_lock(lock_entity_id: str) -> BaseLock | None:
        # Every slot's want goes in with the hold: a new worker reads them all
        # in its first exchange.
        wants = {
            slot_num: coordinator.wants
            for slot_num, coordinator in runtime_data.slot_coordinators.items()
        }
        # Holding waits on the lock's provider setup, which has the operation
        # deadline to answer; said long before that.
        still_waiting = hass.loop.call_later(
            SETUP_WAIT_WARNING_SECONDS,
            _LOGGER.warning,
            "%s (%s): still waiting for %s to answer its setup; its "
            "entities come once it does",
            entry_id,
            entry_title,
            lock_entity_id,
        )
        try:
            lock = await async_hold_lock(hass, config_entry, lock_entity_id, wants)
        except Exception as err:
            # Transport failures degrade inside async_setup_internal, and
            # structural validation failures are logged there and kept
            # degraded, so a popped lock is either a genuine bug or a lock
            # whose provider stopped resolving between selection and setup --
            # an mqtt device re-discovered under an unrecognized bridge. The
            # config flow refuses that selection, so it cannot arrive here
            # from the selection path.
            _LOGGER.error(
                "%s (%s): Failed to set up lock %s: %s",
                entry_id,
                entry_title,
                lock_entity_id,
                err,
                exc_info=err,
            )
            if isinstance(err, UnclaimedLockError):
                # Only this failure has a diagnosis and an action to offer.
                # Any other exception is a bug in a provider LCM does speak,
                # and a repair telling that user their bridge is unsupported
                # sends them to remove a lock that works.
                _async_report_dropped_lock(hass, lock_entity_id, err)
            return None
        finally:
            still_waiting.cancel()
        runtime_data.locks[lock_entity_id] = lock
        # A want that changed while the hold waited -- a condition entity
        # turning, say -- was told only to the locks the entry held then.
        for slot_num, coordinator in runtime_data.slot_coordinators.items():
            if coordinator.wants != wants.get(slot_num):
                coordinator.async_push_want([lock_entity_id])
        _LOGGER.debug("%s (%s): Holding lock %s", entry_id, entry_title, lock_entity_id)
        async_delete_issue(
            hass, DOMAIN, per_lock_issue_id("lock_dropped", lock_entity_id)
        )
        # This lock's entities now, not once every lock is held: holding waits
        # on the lock's provider setup, which a lock that does not answer can
        # stretch to the operation deadline.
        for slot_num in new_config.slot_numbers:
            _LOGGER.debug(
                "%s (%s): Adding lock %s slot %s sensor and event entity",

                entry_title,

                slot_num,

        callbacks.invoke_lock_added_handlers([lock])

    raised: set[str] = set()
    by_slot: dict[int, list[tuple[CredentialAddress, Slot]]] = {}

def _for_slot_1(frame: Frame) -> Answer:
    """Answer slot 1's request with ``frame``; leave every other one to the lock."""

def _applied_once(door_lock: DoorLockStandIn, frame: Frame) -> Answer:
    """
    Apply slot 1's first set or clear as the lock would, but answer it with ``frame``.

    Every later request, and every other slot's, is the lock's own to answer.
    """
    answered: list[int] = []

    def _answer(request: Any) -> Frame | None:
        if request.user_id != 1 or answered:
            return None
        answered.append(request.user_id)
        if request.command.name == "set_pin_code":
            door_lock.codes[request.user_id] = request.pin_code
        else:
            door_lock.codes.pop(request.user_id, None)
        return frame

def _second_virtual_lock(hass: HomeAssistant, provider_entry: MockConfigEntry) -> str:
    """Register another Virtual lock on the provider's entry; return its id."""
    lock_entity = er.async_get(hass).async_get_or_create(
        "lock", "virtual", "test_virtual_2", config_entry=provider_entry
    )
    hass.states.async_set(lock_entity.entity_id, "locked")
    return lock_entity.entity_id


async def _set_up_entry(hass: HomeAssistant, locks: list[str]) -> MockConfigEntry:
    entry = MockConfigEntry(
        domain=DOMAIN,
        data={
            CONF_LOCKS: locks,
            CONF_SLOTS: {
                1: {CONF_NAME: "slot1", CONF_PIN: "1234", CONF_ENABLED: True},
                2: {CONF_NAME: "slot2", CONF_PIN: "5678", CONF_ENABLED: True},
            },
        },
        unique_id="test_password_reconcile",
    )
    entry.add_to_hass(hass)
    assert await hass.config_entries.async_setup(entry.entry_id)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    return entry


async def _submit_locks(hass: HomeAssistant, entry, locks: list[str]) -> None:
    result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_init(entry.entry_id)
    result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_configure(
        result["flow_id"], {CONF_LOCKS: locks}
    )
    assert result["type"] == "create_entry"
    await hass.async_block_till_done()


async def test_removing_every_password_lock_at_once_removes_the_entities(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    virtual_lock_entity,
    virtual_provider_entry,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
) -> None:
    """Two password locks leaving in one submit: no slot keeps the entity."""
    second = _second_virtual_lock(hass, virtual_provider_entry)
    entry = await _set_up_entry(
        hass, [VIRTUAL_LOCK_ENTITY_ID, second, LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]
    )
    assert all(
        CredentialType.PASSWORD in entry.runtime_data.locks[lock].managed_credential_types
        for lock in (VIRTUAL_LOCK_ENTITY_ID, second)
    )
    await entry.runtime_data.slot_coordinators[1].async_request_credential_update(
        CredentialType.PASSWORD, "pw"
    )
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    assert all(_password_entity(hass, entry, slot) is not None for slot in (1, 2))

    await _submit_locks(hass, entry, [LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID])

    assert list(entry.runtime_data.locks) == [LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]
    for slot in (1, 2):
        assert _password_entity(hass, entry, slot) is None
    assert get_entry_config(entry).slot(1)["password"] == "pw"

    await hass.config_entries.async_unload(entry.entry_id)

async def _set_up_entry(hass: HomeAssistant, locks: list[str]) -> MockConfigEntry:
    entry = MockConfigEntry(
        domain=DOMAIN,
        data={
            CONF_LOCKS: locks,
            CONF_SLOTS: {
                1: {CONF_NAME: "slot1", CONF_PIN: "1234", CONF_ENABLED: True},
                2: {CONF_NAME: "slot2", CONF_PIN: "5678", CONF_ENABLED: True},
            },
        },
        unique_id="test_password_reconcile",
    )
    entry.add_to_hass(hass)
    assert await hass.config_entries.async_setup(entry.entry_id)
    await hass.async_block_till_done()
    return entry


async def _submit_locks(hass: HomeAssistant, entry, locks: list[str]) -> None:
    result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_init(entry.entry_id)
    result = await hass.config_entries.options.async_configure(
        result["flow_id"], {CONF_LOCKS: locks}
    )

    await hass.async_block_till_done()


async def test_removing_every_password_lock_at_once_removes_the_entities(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    virtual_lock_entity,
    virtual_provider_entry,
    mock_lock_config_entry,
) -> None:
    """Two password locks leaving in one submit: no slot keeps the entity."""
    second = _second_virtual_lock(hass, virtual_provider_entry)
    entry = await _set_up_entry(
        hass, [VIRTUAL_LOCK_ENTITY_ID, second, LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID]
    )

    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config_entry: LockCodeManagerConfigEntry,
    async_add_entities: AddEntitiesCallback,
) -> bool:
    """Set up config entry."""
    callbacks = config_entry.runtime_data.callbacks
    # Awaited adds: a reconcile that returned has added what it decided to.
    platform = entity_platform.async_get_current_platform()

    @callback
    def add_standard_text_entities(slot_num: int, ent_reg: er.EntityRegistry) -> None:
        """Add a slot's name and PIN; its password is the reconcile's."""
        async_add_entities(
            [
                LockCodeManagerNameText(hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num),
                LockCodeManagerCredentialText(
                    hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num, CredentialType.PIN
                ),
            ],
            True,
            config_subentry_id=subentry_id_for_slot(config_entry, slot_num),
        )

    async def reconcile_password_entities() -> None:
        """
        Give each slot a Password entity exactly when the entry offers passwords.

        The one place that decides, and idempotent: it compares the entities
        that exist with what the entry offers now and acts on the difference.
        Removals are awaited before the additions, so a pass that swaps one
        password lock for another never adds beside an entity still leaving.
        A removed entity's stored password stays (spec decision 10).
        """
        slot_numbers = get_entry_config(config_entry).slot_numbers
        wanted = (
            set(slot_numbers)
            if CredentialType.PASSWORD in available_credential_types(config_entry)
            else set()
        )
        present = {
            slot_num
            for slot_num in slot_numbers
            if _password_uid(slot_num) in callbacks.remove_entity
        }
        for slot_num in sorted(present - wanted):
            await callbacks.async_remove_entity(_password_uid(slot_num))
        ent_reg = er.async_get(hass)
        for slot_num in sorted(wanted - present):
            await platform.async_add_entities(
                [
                    LockCodeManagerCredentialText(
                        hass, ent_reg, config_entry, slot_num, CredentialType.PASSWORD
                    )
                ],
                True,
                config_subentry_id=subentry_id_for_slot(config_entry, slot_num),
            )

    config_entry.async_on_unload(
        callbacks.register_standard_adder(add_standard_text_entities)
    )
    config_entry.async_on_unload(
        callbacks.register_entity_reconciler(reconcile_password_entities)
    )
    return True


def _password_uid(slot_num: int) -> str:
    """Return the removal id a slot's Password entity registers under."""
    return f"{slot_num}|{CredentialType.PASSWORD.value}"

async def test_a_slot_past_capacity_is_no_answer_from_a_dead_lock(ports) -> None:  # noqa: F811
    """
    A read of only slots past the lock's capacity asks the lock nothing.

    The port filters them out and returns {} -- which the worker takes as
    the lock answering. During an outage the probe of the held past-capacity
    slot then "answers": the backoff ends, the owed try of the normal slot is
    paid, and the lock never goes offline. The outage holds a normal slot.
    """
    _, worker, lock = await ports()
    _fast(worker)

    async def capacity(self, slot: int) -> None:
        if slot > 30:
            raise LockOperationUnsupported(f"slot {slot} is past 30")

    with patch.object(type(lock), "_assert_slot_within_capacity", capacity):
        worker.want(pin_address(1), "1111")
        worker.want(pin_address(40), "4040")
        worker.start()
        await worker.settled()
        assert worker.status(pin_address(1)) == (Status.IN_SYNC, None)
        assert worker.status(pin_address(40)) == (Status.SUSPENDED, Repair.CANT_SET)

        # The lock goes dead, and the user changes slot 1's PIN.
        lock.fail("get", error=LockDisconnected)
        lock.fail("set", error=LockDisconnected)
        worker.want(pin_address(1), "2222")
        async with asyncio.timeout(5):
            while not worker.offline and worker.status(pin_address(1))[1] is None:
                await asyncio.sleep(0)

        # An outage alone never holds a normal slot.
        assert worker.status(pin_address(1))[1] is None
        assert worker.offline
        await worker.stop(grace=0.1)


async def test_a_lock_with_only_slots_past_capacity_holds_them_at_once(
    ports,  # noqa: F811
) -> None:
    """Its reads ask nothing: each slot is held, the lock is not taken for gone."""
    _, worker, lock = await ports()
    _fast(worker)

    with patch.object(type(lock), "_assert_slot_within_capacity", capacity):
        worker.want(pin_address(40), "4040")
        worker.start()

        """
        agreed = self.seen is not None and self.agrees(salt)
        self.seen = reading
        if self.agrees(salt):

    def wrote_want(self, salt: bytes) -> None:
        """Record that a write of what is wanted returned without error."""
        self.wrote = self._target(salt)

    def _target(self, salt: bytes) -> str:
        """Return what ``wrote`` holds once what is wanted has been written."""
        return CLEARED if self.want is None else fingerprint(self.want, salt)

    def tried(self) -> None:
        """Count a sync that did not end in sync, with the lock there."""
        self.tries += 1
        if self.tries >= self._limit():
            self.hold, self.liftable = self._give_up(), True

    def fought(self, now: float) -> None:
        """
        Count the lock going from agreeing to disagreeing.

        Agreement never clears these, so a keypad fighting a code back trips

        """
        self.fights = [t for t in self.fights if t > now - WINDOW]
        self.fights.append(now)

content.thinking:
I'm realizing that raising LockOperationUnsupported on a password write immediately produces SLOT_REFUSED then CANT_SET in a single attempt, giving a clean deterministic "fails until suspended" scenario. For Test A, I'm sketching a plan where I patch the system to raise that error for passwords and a CodeRejectedError for PIN "2468", then set a password and verify the worker reports the slot as suspended.

I then realize under the current `_keeps_another_credential` logic, a CANT_SET status would still be treated as "kept" rather than disabled, since it only checks for SLOT_DISABLED — meaning the test would fail with today's code, so I need a combined patch covering both password and PIN failure cases in one scenario. For Test B, I'm working through a case where a PIN-only lock rejects a PIN belonging to a user who also has a password stored on another lock, checking how the worker without a password behaves when the shared user gets disabled.

If a refusal happens on LOCK_1, the user should be turned off everywhere - that's the key decision.

For test D, I want to check that re-enabling clears a slot_disabled issue: use a PIN-only Virtual entry, refuse the PIN to trigger the slot_disabled state, then call the re-enable toggle while still under the refusing patch and confirm the issue is deleted immediately after the enable call, even before things settle - showing re-enabling clears the issue even if the same PIN gets refused again.

The sequence is refuse → settle → off with slot_disabled, then enable → issue immediately None, enabled True, then settle again while still refusing → off again with a fresh slot_disabled issue. If I drop the enable-time deletion logic the second assertion should fail, since the old reconcile-based deletion wouldn't fire when the wanted state still doesn't match after re-enabling.

I should double check whether the enable write triggers an eager sync before my assertion that could re-raise the issue, but since the toggle function itself has no internal awaits, that shouldn't be a problem. Now I need to track down the mock_lock helper and the refuse logic to finish wiring this test up.

async def test_active_toggle_enable_survives_repair_issue_delete_failure(
    hass: HomeAssistant,

    """A failure deleting the credential_required repair issue does not unwind the enable."""
    runtime_data = lock_code_manager_config_entry.runtime_data

    # Disable so the toggle has work to do.

    boom = RuntimeError("issue registry boom")
    with patch(
        "custom_components.lock_code_manager.ha.slot_coordinator.async_delete_issue",
        side_effect=boom,
    ):

            await coordinator.async_request_active_toggle(True)
            await hass.async_block_till_done()

    # Write succeeded; the swallowed delete failure was logged.
    assert coordinator.is_enabled is True
    assert any(
        record.exc_info is not None and record.exc_info[1] is boom
        for record in caplog.records
        if record.levelname == "ERROR"
    )

async def test_a_password_cleared_before_an_error_stays_cleared(
    hass: HomeAssistant, mock_lock_config_entry
):
    """
    The dialog decides once whether it offers a password, on its first form.

    A re-show after an error keeps the field it was drawn with, even if the
    entry's answer changed meanwhile: the user cleared that field.
    """
    entry = _entry_with_users(
        hass,
        [LOCK_1_ENTITY_ID],
        {
            "Ann": {CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1234", "password": "kept"},
            "Bob": {CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "5678"},
        },
        unique_id="offer-changes-on-error",
    )
    subentry = next(
        subentry for subentry in entry.subentries.values() if subentry.title == "Ann"
    )

    with patch(
        "custom_components.lock_code_manager.config_flow._offers_password",
        side_effect=[True, False],
    ):
        result = await hass.config_entries.subentries.async_init(
            (entry.entry_id, SUBENTRY_TYPE_USER),
            context={"source": "reconfigure", "subentry_id": subentry.subentry_id},
        )
        result = await hass.config_entries.subentries.async_configure(
            result["flow_id"],
            {CONF_NAME: "Bob", CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1234"},
        )
        assert result["type"] == "form"
        assert result["errors"]
        assert "password" in {str(key) for key in result["data_schema"].schema}
        with _holding():
            result = await hass.config_entries.subentries.async_configure(
                result["flow_id"],
                {CONF_NAME: "Ann", CONF_ENABLED: True, CONF_PIN: "1234"},
            )

    assert result["type"] == "abort"
    assert not entry.subentries[subentry.subentry_id].data.get("password")

content.text:
**Status:** DONE_WITH_CONCERNS

I did both reworks and the fix as three new commits on `feat/password-config`, nothing amended or pushed. The whole suite passes and `prek run --all-files` is clean. There is one open question at the end about re-enabling a user from the edit form.

## Rework 1: Password entities are reconciled (1f3b8505)

**Removed** (`text.py`):
- The `locks_added` and `lock_removed` handlers and their registrations.
- The `with_password` set, the `add_password_entity` helper and the `discard` on slot add.
- The `ConfigEntryState.LOADED` guard and the "exclude the removed lock" logic.
- The fire-and-forget `config_entry.async_create_task(... async_remove_entity ...)` removal.
- The now-unused imports `ConfigEntryState` and `BaseLock`.
- The standard adder no longer adds the Password entity; it adds only name and PIN.

**Added:**
- `ha/callbacks.py`: `register_entity_reconciler` and `async_reconcile_entities()`. It awaits each registered reconciler in turn and logs one that raises. Its docstring says a capability refresh after setup calls it too, which is the hook for PR 4.
- `text.py`: `reconcile_password_entities()`. It compares the slots that have a Password entity with whether `available_credential_types(entry)` includes passwords. It awaits each removal, then adds the missing entities through the platform's awaitable `async_add_entities` (taken from `entity_platform.async_get_current_platform()`), so an add in the same pass can't race a removal. The stored password stays (decision 10).
- `__init__.py`: one `await callbacks.async_reconcile_entities()` at the end of the update pass, after the locks are released and set up and the new slots have their standard entities. Unload never calls it.

**Tests:**
- New: two Virtual password locks plus the PIN-only mock lock, both password locks removed in one submit. Afterwards no slot has a Password entity and the stored password remains. It failed before the change. A second Virtual lock was easy to build: one more registry entry on the provider entry.
- New: a swap in one submit leaves one live Password entity per slot, with no duplicate unique-id error in `caplog`. It already passed before the change; the race didn't show up in the test harness.
- New: a unit test of the reconciler registry in `tests/test_callbacks.py`.
- Changed: `test_a_second_password_lock_adds_no_second_entity` called the lock-added handler directly, which no longer does anything for text. It is now `test_reconciling_again_adds_no_second_entity` and calls the reconcile twice. Its assertions are unchanged.

**Mutation:** I moved the reconcile from the end of the pass to each lock's removal and arrival. The multi-removal test and `test_the_password_entity_leaves_with_the_last_password_lock` failed. File restored.

## Rework 2: the refusal rule asks the lock's worker (681bf677)

**Removed:**
- `_keeps_another_credential` in `ha/runtime.py`: the configuration read through `coordinator.wants` and the exception for credentials the same lock refused.
- The in-sync `slot_disabled` deletion in `async_reconcile_issues` (the `wanted` predicate). Nothing else needed it.
- `test_a_refusal_is_answered_while_another_types_clear_is_held`, added earlier in this PR.
- `TestSlotRepairs::test_a_refusals_repair_is_answered_beside_a_password_that_wants_nothing` in `tests/providers/virtual/test_e2e.py`. This test is on main (from #1770). Both tests checked that the reconcile answers `slot_disabled`, which no longer happens, so I removed them as scenarios that no longer make sense rather than forcing them.

**Added:**
- `_another_credential_works(worker, address)`: true only if another address of the same slot on that lock's worker has a non-None want and status `IN_SYNC`.
- The coordinator's successful enable (`async_request_active_toggle(True)`) now deletes `slot_disabled_{entry}_{slot}` beside `credential_required`, in one loop that logs a registry failure for either.
- Comments updated in `runtime.py` and `sync/slot.py`.

**Tests** (in `test_password_config.py`; the first three new ones failed before the change):
- A suspended password is no fallback. The password write raises `LockOperationUnsupported`, so it is held `CANT_SET` at once; then the PIN is refused and the user is turned off.
- A credential the refusing lock doesn't take is no fallback. On an entry with Virtual and the PIN-only mock lock, the password is in sync on Virtual and absent from the mock lock's worker; the mock lock refuses the PIN and the user is turned off.
- Re-enable answers `slot_disabled`. Refused PIN: the user is off with the issue. Re-enable: the user is on and the issue is gone. Refused again: the user is off with a fresh issue. I assert after each step.
- The existing "refused password while the PIN works" test still passes.

**Mutations** (files restored after each):

| Mutation | Test that failed |
|---|---|
| Count a non-`IN_SYNC` address as a fallback | the suspended test |
| Read the configuration instead of the worker | the doesn't-take test (and the suspended test) |
| Drop the enable-time deletion | the re-enable test |

## Fix 3: the edit form decides "offered" once per dialog (d14d5398)

**Changed:** `_password_offered` is now `bool | None = None` (it was `bool = False`). `_async_show_reconfigure` computes it only while it is `None`, so a re-show after an error keeps the first answer. A submit with no form drawn still keeps the stored password.

**Test:** `test_a_password_cleared_before_an_error_stays_cleared` in `tests/test_config_flow.py` patches `_offers_password` to answer True then False. The user clears the password and submits a clashing name; the re-shown form still has the field; the corrected submit leaves the password cleared.

**Mutation:** recomputing on every show makes that test fail. File restored.

## Test runs
- Full suite with `-n auto`: 3544 passed, 3 skipped, 14 xfailed. The only failures were the three known paced tests (`TestPacing`, `test_pins_changed_while_the_lock_is_offline_reach_it_once_each_paced`, `test_a_paced_test_keeps_the_real_delay_between_operations`); re-run on their own, all 4 passed.
- `prek run --all-files` passes. Every commit passed prek, including mypy.

## Concerns
- **Re-enabling from the edit form leaves `slot_disabled` behind.** The edit (reconfigure) form writes `enabled: True` without going through `async_request_active_toggle`, so re-enabling there no longer deletes the issue. Before this change the reconcile deletion covered that path. `credential_required` already had the same gap. A single spot that would catch every way of re-enabling is `notify_config_changed` seeing enabled go from off to on; that's a design choice for you to make.
- **A Password entity the user disabled in the registry is never added**, so it never registers for removal, and the reconcile can't remove its registry entry later. The old handlers had the same limit.
- **Later reconcile callers should hold the entry's pass lock.** The update pass calls the reconcile under it; PR 4 calling it on a capability refresh should take it too, to stay serialized with passes.

Mutation scripts are in `/tmp/lcm-rework-mut/`. The main checkout was not touched, and the pre-existing `.entire/.gitignore` change is still unstaged.

content.thinking:
I'm identifying `_recompute_active` as the central chokepoint for all config changes, and planning to add a transition check before its early-unchanged-return. I'll track a `_was_enabled` flag so I can detect the moment a slot flips from disabled to enabled and trigger the appropriate callback there.

First compute is treated as "no transition" since `_was_enabled` starts as `None`, and I want to reset it to `None` in `async_start` so stop/start cycles on the same coordinator don't falsely register a transition. I'm also second-guessing whether the credential_required repair could linger incorrectly in the edit-form path where a slot is already enabled and just gets a credential added, since that path doesn't go through an off→on transition.

Tracing through the slot-disabled flow: the toggle-off task runs eagerly and writes enabled=False before the issue gets created, so re-enabling afterward triggers a proper transition and deletes the issue correctly. I also want to check how notify_config_changed recomputes things without false transitions, and I should look at existing tests like the one for toggle-enable surviving repair-issue delete failures to make sure my changes to the toggle deletion loop don't break them.

For the delete-failure case, I need the recompute hook to log and swallow exceptions from async_delete_issue rather than propagate them, so enabled stays True and the error is just logged.

I'm planning a new test: force a PIN refusal to create the disabled issue, then submit an edit-form re-enable (without the refusal patch active) and verify the issue clears and enabled becomes True — confirming the deletion only works because of the hook, not leftover reconcile logic.

- Home Assistant caps a text entity's value at 255 characters (`MAX_LENGTH_STATE_STATE`): `TextEntity.max` is `min(native_max, 255)`, and both `text.set_value` and `state` raise a `ValueError` that quotes the value. content.text:
**Status:** DONE

Re-enabling a user by any route, the edit form included, now deletes both `slot_disabled` and `credential_required`. That is one more commit, **e4fd1159**, on top of 31cdae3c: nothing amended or pushed. The full suite passes, apart from the known paced flakes, which pass on their own.

## What changed (`ha/slot_coordinator.py`)
- **Added:** the coordinator remembers the enabled flag its last compute saw. `_recompute_active` is the one place every change passes through: `async_start`, `notify_config_changed`, `_write_config_fields` and condition changes all call it.
  - When the flag goes from off to on, it calls a new `_answer_enable_repairs()`, which deletes both issues. A registry failure is logged and doesn't undo the enable.
  - The check runs before the method's "nothing changed" early return, because enabled can flip while the active state stays the same.
  - The remembered flag starts empty and is cleared again in `async_start`, so a coordinator starting up deletes nothing.
- **Removed:** both deletions in `async_request_active_toggle(True)`, the existing `credential_required` one and the `slot_disabled` one I added in 681bf677.

## Tests
- **New:** `test_re_enabling_in_the_edit_form_answers_slot_disabled`. A refused PIN turns the user off and raises `slot_disabled`. Re-enabling through the edit form deletes the issue at once; once the PIN reaches the lock, the issue stays gone. It failed before the change.
- **Existing tests run explicitly, all passing:**
  - switch: `test_switch_entity`, which asserts `credential_required` is deleted on turn-on;
  - coordinator: `test_request_active_toggle_clears_credential_required_issue`, `test_request_active_toggle_blocks_when_no_pin`, `test_active_toggle_enable_survives_repair_issue_delete_failure`;
